subject: mathematics
question_text: Draw the graph of y = cos²x on (0, π).

mark_split.label: Table of values and the range

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.87, chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 28(ii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The split gives one mark to the table of values together with the range 0 ≤ y ≤ 1 and one to the drawing itself, since the question asks for a graph. recall_prompt: Say how you would draw this one — name the values you plot, the range, and the shape you get.

steps.label: Table of values and the range
steps.margin_note: First mark. Writing cos²x as (1 + cos 2x)/2 settles two things at once: the values stay between 0 and 1, and the pattern repeats every π.
steps.memory_tip: cos²x = (1 + cos 2x)/2, so y stays between 0 and 1 and the pattern repeats every π.
lines: The curve falls from 1 to 0 at x = π/2,
then rises back to 1 at x = π.

recall.must_convey: That cos²x = (1 + cos 2x)/2 so 0 ≤ y ≤ 1, and that the values at 0, π/4, π/2, 3π/4, π are 1, 1/2, 0, 1/2, 1.
accept: cos squared x is one plus cos two x over two so y lies between zero and one
at zero it is one, at pi by four it is a half and at pi by two it is zero
the values are one, half, zero, half, one
cos square x ni half of one plus cos two x ga rasi range zero to one
make the table and note that the value never goes below zero

steps.why: A square is never negative, so the curve never goes below the x-axis. Knowing that before drawing stops the usual mistake of copying the shape of cos x.
common_mistakes: Drawing the shape of cos x, which goes down to −1.

steps.label: Draw the graph
steps.margin_note: Second mark, and the point of the question. One smooth dip: start at height 1, touch the x-axis at x = π/2 and come back up to 1 at x = π. The interval is open, so the value 1 is approached at the two ends but not included.
steps.memory_tip: One dip only: down from 1 to 0 at π/2 and back up to 1 at π. It never crosses the x-axis.

recall.must_convey: That the axes are drawn and one smooth dip is sketched from 1 down to 0 at x = π/2 and back to 1 at x = π, staying on or above the x-axis. Naming the drawing is full credit.
accept: draw the axes and one dip from one down to zero at pi by two and back to one
sketch the curve touching the x axis at pi by two
draw a single valley between zero and pi that never goes below the axis
axes geesi, pi by two daggara zero touch chesi malli one ki ravali
draw the graph as one dip above the x axis

steps.why: The curve TOUCHES the x-axis at x = π/2 and turns back; it does not cross. That single contact point is what shows the smallest value is 0 and not a negative number.
common_mistakes: Letting the curve go below the x-axis.
Drawing two dips, which is the graph of cos²x over an interval of length 2π.
Making the curve cross the axis at π/2 instead of touching it.
